topology: Two AMD EPYC 7773X hosts. Head on Milan, HDB and load on Tinkara. Local NVMe WAL and HDB, NFSv4 Parquet handoff. Two native subscribers in the load pod.
clients: Native kg processes matched to each server build. Python schedules trials and validates SQL and subscriber totals.
source: Journal-only script and all harness inputs in the tuned source revision. For the Rust arm use the head.kg and .tickerwal from its source revision.
micro_order: At each of 8, 1024 and 98304 rows: rust, klong, klong, rust. In the second series: tuned, klong, klong, tuned. Fresh directory for each sample; same repeated precomputed four-column payload, sync per batch. Replay validation includes Klong comparisons and final EOF sync; warm file cache.
wal_identity: Daily WAL compared byte for byte against the Rust output at all three batch sizes; identical.
cpu_counters: Interior 0.5-second samples. NIC counters include all host traffic. HDB and load share a NIC. CPU in cores; peak sampled cgroup memory includes file cache.
recovery_method: Copied the large-batch Klong 12-second probe WAL into a fresh directory on local NVMe. Initialized its day and first sequence, appended one sentinel and confirmed its watermark. On each of two SIGKILL trials the clock started before kill and stopped after a fresh IPC client received the expected latest sentinel and watermark. Verified total live row count afterwards. Linux page cache warm, head only.
